• *Glans* (“head”): rounded tip covered by mucous membrane called the foreskin when present.
• *Urethral opening*: located at the distal end of the glans, through which urine and semen exit. | | **Blood Supply** | Arterial inflow via branches of the internal pudendal artery; venous drainage primarily through the deep dorsal vein and superficial veins. | | **Nerve Supply** | Sensory innervation largely from the dorsal nerve of the penis (a branch of the pudendal nerve). Autonomic fibers control smooth muscle relaxation/contraction during erection and detumescence. | | **Primary Functions** | 1. **Urination** – passage of urine from bladder to outside body.

Smooth muscle relaxation prevents backflow until orgasmic climax. | | **Common Conditions** | - Erectile dysfunction
- Peyronie’s disease (fibrous plaque causing curvature)
